## RCA (Phase 1 — confirmed root cause)

**Mechanism (proven).** `run_access_check` (`access_check.py`) drives the six-step probe inside one
`try` whose only failure handler is a broad `except Exception as exc` catch-all
(`access_check.py:237-242`). At `STEP_CREATE` it calls `client.create_issue(...)`, which for the
acli transport ultimately reaches `subprocess.Popen(["acli", ...])` in
`adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:_run_acli` (line ~556). When the `acli` binary is absent/unresolvable,
`Popen` raises `FileNotFoundError([Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli')`. That infrastructure
fault is indistinguishable, at the catch-all, from an in-band provider failure, so it is stringified
verbatim into the step verdict as `reason=exception, detail="[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli'"`.

**Discriminating experiment (runtime).** Drove `run_access_check(env=…, client_cls=MissingAcliClient)`
where `MissingAcliClient.create_issue` raises the exact `FileNotFoundError(2, "No such file or directory", "acli")`
that a missing binary produces. Observed verdict `FAIL` / rc 1 with:
`steps=[{"step":"STEP_CREATE","passed":false,"reason":"exception","detail":"[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'acli'"}]`
— reproducing the report exactly. This confirms the raw errno leak at the catch-all and rules out
any typed-mapping already being in place on this path.

**Contrast — the sibling that DOES type it (parity reference).** The mapped-project visibility preflight
in the same module already represents an unreachable transport typed: `TransportUnavailableError`
(`access_check.py:301`) and `ProjectVisibilityResult.status == "transport_unavailable"`
(`_build_probe_client`/`fetch_visible_project_keys`/`check_mapped_project_visibility`, e.g. lines 340/389/467/486).
The STEP_CREATE probe never adopted that vocabulary.

**Defect legitimacy = defect (preexisting omission).** The intended-behavior authority is the module's
own established typed transport-unavailable vocabulary (the sibling path above) plus the closed P1 parent
`54e6-ecb0` (raw acli-missing surfacing was a real defect) — this ticket is its AC#4 alternative branch.
A missing transport binary is an infrastructure fault that must map to a typed transport-unavailable
verdict, not a raw errno string. Unlocks Phase 2 (fix wraps the error only; verdict/returncode unchanged).

**Attribution — `caused_by = f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d` (class: plan_defect).**
Blame of the leak lines (237-242), the `STEP_CREATE` init (171), and `git log -S`/`--follow --diff-filter=A`
all point to the single introducing commit `fa1bf138455b` ("Expose bridge operations through library and MCP",
2026-08-10), ticket **f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d**, which created `access_check.py` and its broad catch-all. The
exception-leak string exists in **no other commit** in history. Date test: the leak predates the typed
`TransportUnavailableError` contract (commit `9eb8c34`, 2026-08-15) — i.e. the site was deficient from birth,
never a regression — so the origin is the plan that shipped the probe without a missing-transport case, not
the later typed-vocab commit (that is only the remedy pattern this fix reuses). This is a considered
attribution to a producer/plan omission, deliberately NOT the whole-file blame default (which would also
land on fa1bf138 here, so they agree).
